results.name: medium-core-off-baseline
results.title: Baseline · STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
results.action: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions, read back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state, and send three ARP broadcasts each way. No fault is applied.

phases.name: Baseline
phases.expected: Both MLAG peers run protocol-mode=none with forward-reserved-addresses=no, so they neither send BPDUs nor pass the access switch's BPDUs (STP group address 01:80:C2:00:00:00). The access switch is the only RSTP bridge and, with priority 0x0000, its own root (root ID 0x0000.02:00:00:21:00:13). Its uplink bond is an edge port, so it forwards at once without a proposal/agreement handshake, and its host port ether4 is an edge port with bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on. MLAG is connected, every bond member is synchronized, collecting and distributing, each ARP broadcast arrives once and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

results.name: medium-core-off-power-loss-primary
results.title: MLAG primary power loss · Medium lab, STP off on the MLAG pair, RSTP on the access switch (campus option 1)
results.action: Resets the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH: protocol-mode=none and forward-reserved-addresses=no on both MLAG peers, protocol-mode=rstp priority=0x0000 on the access switch, with edge=yes on its uplink bond and edge=yes, bpdu-guard=yes and loop-protect=on on its host port ether4, and reads the access switch port settings back. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, no BPDU from or through the MLAG pair and one copy of each broadcast. It then emulates a power loss of CHR 1 (MLAG primary): in one step it takes the container veths behind CHR 1's ether2 to ether4 down, sets the facing NICs of CHR 2 and the access switch link-down over QMP and pauses CHR 1's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers CHR 1 on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

phases.name: Primary off
phases.expected: Every link to CHR 1 loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. CHR 2 sees its peer port ether2 go down and reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID, so the access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. They drop their member to CHR 1 on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout. The access switch's uplink is an edge port, so it forwards as soon as LACP has reselected.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: Carrier returns while CHR 1 boots. CHR 1 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID. The access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP to the shared system ID with brief loss, and the edge uplink forwards again at once.
